goals: Route acquired items into supported unlocked carried shulkers using exact physical matching contents or matching empty CSR reservations, preserving component identity, effective capacities, counts, and existing global destination order.
Preserve established passive-pickup, external QUICK_MOVE, and player-origin QUICK_MOVE behavior across vanilla and Inventory Extended storage while composing safely with Offhand Shift-Click QoL.
Provide a server-authoritative lock control that excludes selected carriers from automatic routing without altering their other contents or components.

Extend Survival Pick Block only after vanilla ordinary-inventory failure, retrieving the exact matching physical stack from an unlocked carried shulker and atomically re-homing the displaced hotbar stack without changing Creative behavior, routing locks, or CSR reservations.
scope: Canonical 0.3.15-shulker-pick-block-canary1 for Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric, implementation checkpoint dbb8f82aeee2c0f3357f93867c517e05d43ed5a5; server-authoritative Survival Pick Block successor validated with optional CSR Canary 19.

Minecraft 26.2 ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.tryPickItem remains the sole block/entity Pick Block authority. Vanilla Inventory.findSlotMatchingItem runs first with ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents; existing hotbar selection or Inventory.pickSlot behavior wins unchanged. Only a Survival/Adventure NOT_FOUND result enters CCAR, while Creative, spectator, and client-side calls remain vanilla-owned.

CCAR searches only supported unlocked carried shulkers in its established physical ordinary-inventory order followed by offhand, and each shulker's physical slots 0 through 26. Bundles, unsupported carriers, locked hosts, and recursive nested-container contents are excluded. The entire physical matching source stack moves, matching vanilla Inventory.pickSlot quantity semantics, and Inventory.getSuitableHotbarSlot selects the destination.

Before mutation, Pick Block snapshots the complete live ordinary-storage list, offhand, selected slot, source host/slot/stack, displaced stack, every compatible-partial allocation, optional first empty ordinary slot, and exact-source-slot fallback. A second exact count-and-component validation precedes the first live write; stale state or an incomplete legal destination aborts without mutation.

Displacement planning preserves CCAR's compatible-destination priority after the selected slot: unlocked carried-shulker partials in shared carrier/physical order, remaining hotbar partials, occupied matching offhand, and complete live ordinary-storage partials. It respects component identity, effective maxima, nesting, routing locks, native admission, and CSR admission, and never establishes empty-slot shulker affinity.

After compatible partials, the first empty live ordinary-inventory slot in vanilla index order receives any remainder. Only when no such slot exists may the exact physical shulker source slot receive the remainder, and only if native/CSR admission and effective capacity permit it; a conflicting source reservation therefore fails the entire planned transaction atomically.

When a server-resolved routing-lock target is unsupported, return without an overlay message. Preserve server-authoritative supported-target toggles and their existing Locked/Unlocked feedback exactly.

Passive ground pickup and external-container QUICK_MOVE priority through component-identical occupied main hand, qualifying carried containers, occupied hotbar, occupied offhand, compatible ordinary-storage partials, empty hotbar, and empty ordinary storage.
Player-origin QUICK_MOVE routing to a component-identical occupied offhand and qualifying carried containers before returning exact remainder ownership to the active menu's normal algorithm.
Creative and Survival inventory snapshot alignment, source cleanup and menu callbacks, exact remainder accounting, stable carrier order, and persistent per-carrier auto-routing lock state.

Only the shared ShulkerDestination changes routing admission: physical component-exact matches seed affinity unless their reservation conflicts; full matching physical stacks retain affinity. Physically empty RESERVED_MATCH slots also seed affinity. Empty unreserved, unrelated, locked, and nesting-prohibited destinations remain ineligible.

Read only ContainerSlotReservationsApi.classify(ItemStack,int,ItemStack), isReserved(ItemStack,int), reservationMatches(ItemStack,int,ItemStack), and the client-only ShulkerPanelHeaderDecorations API after FabricLoader confirms CSR is loaded. CSR remains suggests *: direct header API linkage is isolated in a reflection-loaded client bridge, absent/incompatible linkage leaves CCAR fully functional without a badge.

Build one immutable slot/count plan before mutation: compatible occupied stacks in physical order, all matching reserved empties in physical order, then unreserved empties in physical order. Rewrite CONTAINER once and shrink the incoming stack by exactly the accepted total; retain reservations, lock, name, lore, damage, and unrelated components.

Keep accepted bundle class bytes unchanged, global destination and carrier order unchanged, all existing pickup/QUICK_MOVE contexts, offhand/excluded-source behavior, and Stacks Are Stacks effective maximums without a new stack-size implementation.

When optional CSR is present, expose the existing RoutingLock state for supported shulkers only as a clickable 1:1 supplied lock sprite in CSR's header. CCAR owns its optional provider action and sends ToggleLockPayload for the exact bound live menu slot; CSR never links to CCAR or mutates RoutingLock. The server accepts only current, active, non-fake, modifiable legitimate menu slots, then resolves the supported carrier from that exact server stack. Bundles remain tooltip-only. C16 derives its direct resources from C15's immutable supplied locked.png (7x9, 155 bytes, SHA-256 cde847dba65a29823d62fee4f70fc4c1e83fd40e4fbbc4b81871b9164f11e617, opaque RGBA) and unlocked.png (10x9, 590 bytes, SHA-256 10a5f3205c311974eea2798e1c97cca248798f12b7156c202c59afbb850fc39c, opaque RGBA): only exact opaque #FFFFFFFF pixels become #00000000, producing locked SHA-256 bbe0d7393b626c1bc2d6b7d9f938888d4a99ae130eb90ecd2cb5711a909e226d and unlocked SHA-256 a87026fa1ab3a82cf76cd0dd5a68cf79fa49ef2e0fbfed27964ad18c7d48c656. Direct package integrity checks prove the 29 non-white opaque pixels and all dimensions remain exact; no crop or generated-art pipeline remains.

For a WORLD_PICKUP only, C18 compares the actual incoming count around the established routing call, records actual carried shulker or bundle insertion separately, and marks when vanilla reaches Player.take. A missing vanilla take sends exactly one collector-only local ITEM_PICKUP sound at the captured item position; normal custom movement uses the Minecraft 26.2 random pitch and carried movement uses that pitch times 0.80. A reached vanilla take retains C17's one-shot entity-ID marker and no fallback. QUICK_MOVE and nonaccepting, locked, full, or nonqualifying carriers never signal either cue.

exclusions: Equipment, Trinkets, trash, and foreign menu slots remain excluded.
No generic automatic backpack: an empty unreserved shulker or a nonmatching reservation cannot establish affinity; locked carriers and forbidden nesting remain denied.

Pick Block is not a sorter or generic extractor: it does not search bundles, recurse into nested containers, create arbitrary empty-shulker affinity, bypass reservations, or alter Creative Pick Block.
No internal CSR persistence access, reservation mutation, fake stacks, runtime CSR pin, foreign classes, or nested CSR/upstream JAR.
No modifications to bundles, global destination/carrier order, accepted C11/rollback C10 bytes, QSN C8, SAS C2, Easy Shulker Boxes, Item Interactions, or other project implementations.
No successor runtime pass/promotion inferred from controlled tests; no dedicated Minecraft launch or protected gameplay-profile access.
